problem: The Euler criterion as stated is false for graphs with isolated vertices (they have Euler tours but are not connected); what is needed is that all edges lie in one component.
corrected: \text{tree on } n \text{ vertices} \iff \text{connected with } n-1 \text{ edges}
\text{Euler tour exists} \iff \text{all degrees even and all edges in one component}

problem: Dirac's theorem needs n >= 3: K_2 has minimum degree 1 = n/2 but no cycle.
ex(n, K_{r+1}) equals (1-1/r) n^2/2 only when r divides n; in general it is t(n,r), the edge count of the Turán graph, which is at most that value.
